title: NRL Referee Salary: Converting Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay with a 38-Hour Week
description: Learn how to convert an NRL referee salary or any hourly rate to annual pay using a 38-hour week, 52-week year, plus tax and super. Fair Work rates included.
salarySummary: For a full-time 38-hour week, annual gross pay is hourly rate × 38 × 52; the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44/hour, giving $52,254.80 per year before tax and super.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time week of 38 hours, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual pay before tax and super. The same method applies whether you are checking an NRL referee salary or any other hourly wage.

faqs.q: What is the 38-hour week and why is it used?
faqs.a: The 38-hour week is the standard full-time working week under many modern awards in Australia, including the National Minimum Wage order. It is also the basis for the Fair Work Ombudsman's pay guides and the Fair Work Commission's Modern Awards Pay Database. Using 38 hours ensures consistency when comparing annual pay across different awards.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect my pay calculation?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an additional 25% on top of the base hourly rate, intended to compensate for lack of paid leave. When using the calculator, enter your base hourly rate (without casual loading) and check the casual loading box to add 25%. bodyMarkdown:
## Converting an Hourly Rate to Annual Pay

Whether you are checking an **NRL referee salary** or any other hourly wage, the conversion to annual pay follows a simple formula: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**. This gives your gross annual earnings before tax and superannuation. For a standard full-time week, we assume **38 hours** – the benchmark used in most modern awards and by the Fair Work Commission.

### The 38-Hour Week and the Fortnight

A 38-hour week is the standard full-time working week under many awards, including the National Minimum Wage order. To find your fortnightly pay, simply multiply your weekly pay by 2. For example, if your weekly pay is $1,004.90 (the National Minimum Wage for 38 hours), your fortnightly pay is $2,009.80. This helps with budgeting and aligns with common pay cycles.

### Award Rates and the National Minimum Wage

The Fair Work Commission publishes the Modern Awards Pay Database which contains minimum rates, allowances, and penalty rates for each award. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides pay guides that summarise these rates. From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is **$26.44 per hour**, or **$1,004.90 per week** for 38 hours. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making the casual rate **$33.05 per hour**. These figures are the legal minimums – many awards and enterprise agreements set higher rates.

### NRL Referee Salary – An Example

While the search results do not provide a specific NRL referee salary, the conversion method applies to any hourly rate. If an NRL referee earns a hypothetical hourly rate of, say, $50.00, their annual gross pay would be $50 × 38 × 52 = **$98,800**. Actual NRL referee pay may be set by an enterprise agreement or a professional sports award. You can check the Fair Work Ombudsman's pay guides or the Modern Awards Pay Database for applicable rates. The key point: the formula works for any hourly wage, whether it's an NRL referee salary or a retail assistant's rate.

### Tax and Superannuation

Once you have your gross annual pay, you can estimate tax using the 2026–27 resident tax rates: nil on the first $18,200, 15% on the next $26,800 (to $45,000), 30% on the next $90,000 (to $135,000), 37% on the next $55,000 (to $190,000), and 45% above that. The Medicare levy adds 2% (based on 2025–26 single thresholds). Superannuation guarantee is **12% of ordinary earnings**, paid on top of your salary, up to a maximum contribution base of $270,830. For example, on a $98,800 annual salary, super would be an additional $11,856 per year.

### Casual Loading

If you work casually, remember that the 25% loading is added to your base rate. Our calculator includes a checkbox to add casual loading automatically. **Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading** – always start with the base hourly rate. The loading is then applied on top.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay calculated here assumes the same hourly rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax. For personalised advice, consult a qualified professional.

### Using the Calculator

To get started, visit [the timesheet](/) and enter your base hourly rate. Check the casual loading box if applicable. The calculator will show your weekly, fortnightly, and annual pay, along with estimated tax and super. You can also explore [pay guides](/blog) for award-specific rates or [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) information.
